title: G2M vertical hypothesis notes + microcopy
content:
Purpose
- Quick working notes for messaging tests and positioning experiments across five verticals: fintech, healthcare, legal, enterprise SaaS, gov/defense.
- Deliverables: 1-page variant microcopy for A/B tests, competitor signal bullets, prioritized experiments for Q2.
- Audience: growth + product + solutions leads who will run creative experiments and sales talk tracks.

Summary thesis (one-liner)
- Carve the ‘serving-first’ slice of value: for regulated and reliability-sensitive verticals, we position Redwood as the inference runtime that turns ML models into predictable operational outcomes (latency, cost, auditability) instead of just model access.

Key positioning pillars (shared across verticals)
1) Predictable economics at scale — dedicated pools, autoscale policies, intelligent batching.
2) Observable and auditable inference — token-level traces, request replay, KMS/HSM integrations.
3) Operational fallbacks and availability — model variant routing, cross-region failover, SLA-backed capacity.
4) Developer ergonomics + enterprise controls — same API across hosted/dedicated/private; rollout tools and canaries.

Notes on tone and microcopy approach
- Keep customer-facing lines outcome-oriented, not platform-first. Example: avoid “we provide quantization profiles”; prefer “cut inference costs by 2–4x without measurable drop in accuracy.”
- For security/regulatory audiences (healthcare, gov), lead with controls and evidence (SOC2, audit logs, private control plane).
- For fintech/legal, use trust-language (traceability, rollback, deterministic prompts).
- Microcopy variants should be short (10–20 words) for hero lines + 1–2 supporting bullets.

Vertical: Fintech (payments, risk, wealth platforms)
Audience pain: latency spikes during market events, cost unpredictability with bursty workloads, audit/regulatory demands for deterministic logs.
Competitive signal map (who says what)
- General cloud LLM APIs: "fast, simple pricing," but little enterprise SLAs or isolation.
- Inference vendors/self-host: "full control," but heavy ops and slower dev velocity.
- Our gap/opportunity: combine predictable reserved capacity + low-friction API + traceable request paths.
Sample hero lines (A/B variants)
A: "Serve trading & fraud models with 99.9% predictable latency — even at market peaks."
B: "Reduce inference cost and stay audit-ready — reserved capacity + token-level traces."
Supporting bullets
- Autoscale policies that respect cost vs latency SLOs.
- Query-level audit trails for compliance and RM reporting.
Early experiments (in priority order)
1) Hero copy A/B on fintech landing + CTA to latency SLO page. Track signup -> trial use with simulated bursts. (KR: +10% conversion from dev signups to reserved-commit trials)
2) Case study skeleton with sample numbers: cost/unit before/after quantization + latency percentiles.
Open questions / risks
- What concrete regulatory phrases can we use without implying certifications? (Legal to review)
- Need benchmark data for payments-scale bursts — ask SRE for 1-week traces.

Vertical: Healthcare (SaaS EMR, clinical decision support)
Audience pain: PHI handling, audit trails, on-prem/vpc requirements, explainability/regulatory traceability.
Competitive signals
- Cloud vendors highlight private networking and compliance docs but lack inference economics tooling.
- On-prem inference stacks require ops heavy lifting and lack dev ergonomics.
Positioning focus
- Private control-plane + optional air-gapped on-prem bundle + audit hooks = reduces compliance lift for AI features.
Microcopy variants
A: "Ship PHI-safe LLM features with private deployment and built-in audit trails."
B: "From dev sandbox to on-prem production — maintain privacy and consistent performance."
Support bullets
- KMS/HSM integrations and tenant-level key controls.
- Token-level request logs and replay for QA/regulatory review.
Experiments (quick wins)
- Run a gated demo showing data residency toggles + sample audit trail export. Invite 6 HIPAA customers for feedback.
- Copy test on product pages aimed at clinical informatics teams.

Vertical: Legal (document review, contract analysis)
Audience pain: correctness/regression risk, DR/rollback, ability to pin model versions and see behavior changes over time.
Competitive signals
- Legal tech vendors bundle models with UI but often lack clear service guarantees or verifiable logs.
Opportunity
- Sell framework: reproducible inference + versioned model rollouts + eval hooks for prompt sets.
Microcopy variants
A: "Pin model versions, replay requests, and surface regressions before they become a liability."
B: "Make LLM-driven reviews auditable and reversible — built for law firms and legal teams."
Support bullets
- Per-prompt evals and quality regression alerts tied to golden prompt sets.
- Canary rollouts and automatic fallback to older model variants.
Experiment ideas
- Create a short checklist + sales cheat sheet for conversations with legal teams (what to show in a demo).

Vertical: Enterprise SaaS (product teams adding LLM features)
Audience pain: cost leakage, unpredictable latency impacting UX, lack of observability in production.
Competitive signals
- SaaS platform vendors promise simple APIs; customers hit surprise bills and sudden latency.
Opportunity + message
- Redwood as the predictable runtime: same API, predictable bills, observability for product KPIs.
Microcopy
A: "Give product teams predictable costs and predictable latency — ship LLM features with confidence."
B: "Instrument every model call; tie inference metrics back to product KPIs (DAU, churn, time-to-value)."
Support bullets
- Token-level cost attribution so PMs know which features drive costs.
- Rollout and canary UX for safe experiments in production.
Experiment
- Small UX copy change in billing/usage view: show per-feature per-day cost estimate. Measure PM adoption of cost controls.

Vertical: Gov & Defense (classified/unclassified separation)
Audience pain: air-gapped requirements, procurement cycles, NIST/CC standards, procurement language.
Competitive signals
- Procurement-heavy vendors lean on bespoke integration; cloud providers point to compliance offerings.
Our approach
- Position as engineering partner that can deliver air-gapped private deployments and provide red-team-friendly attestations.
Microcopy (very conservative)
A: "Private inference deployments — designed for sensitive workloads and procurement readiness."
B: "We integrate with your PKI and network controls; we operate on your terms."
Support bullets
- On-prem distribution + hardened audit logs.
- Compliance intake playbook for procurement teams.
Experiments
- Create a 1-pager procurement brief tailored for federal buyers. Share with two channel partners for feedback.

Cross-vertical competitive notes (short)
- Core competitors: managed cloud LLM APIs (lower friction), self-hosted inference vendors (high control), and consulting outfits (integration-heavy).
- Key signal buyers watch: SLA language, proof of uptime under bursts, audit trace examples, sample invoices showing unit economics.

Objections & rebuttals (playbook snippets)
- "Why not just host our own inference?" -> "That’s feasible, but costs and ops scale quickly; we provide predictable commit options + engineers tooling to reduce ops load and time-to-value."
- "How do we prove cost savings?" -> "We provide model-by-model before/after simulations and token-level cost reports; run a 30-day pilot with controlled traffic."

KPIs for these experiments
- Conversion: dev signups -> reserved trial commits (target +15% vs baseline)
- Demo -> proof-of-concept to purchase velocity (target: shorten by 20%)
- Messaging lift: click-through on hero variants (target +8–12%)

Next steps / owner action items
- Growth: stage A/B test for fintech and enterprise-saas hero variants. (Owner: Leah)
- Product: produce benchmark packets for payments-scale bursts and HIPAA demo telemetry. (Owner: Owen)
- Solutions: draft procurement 1-pager for gov/defense. (Owner: Priya)
- Legal: review regulated phrasing and compliance statements. (Owner: Marcus)

Open research requests
- SRE: one-week traces of peak trading/burst traffic, plus cost breakouts by model size.
- Applied ML: typical accuracy deltas for 4-bit/8-bit quantization on our common model family.

Notes to self (brainstorm fragments)
- Consider a small interactive demo: slider that toggles reserved capacity vs burst and shows simulated latency/cost curves. Great for sales and landing.
- Could we publish a short ‘inference economics by vertical’ PDF with sample numbers? High value for field marketing.

Unresolved questions
- Are there existing customer stories we can anonymize for fintech/healthcare? Need success team input.
- How much we can claim about certifications/certified partners? (legal + security check)

Appendix: sample short emails (for SDRs)
- Fintech lead variant: "Quick note — we helped a trading platform keep latency under 40ms during market opens while cutting inference spend by ~30%. Can we share a short packet?"
- Healthcare lead variant: "We offer a private control plane + token-level audit trails to help teams move from POC to HIPAA-ready production faster."

-- end of draft --
